0.0.n: 自分 refers to the speaker here, rather than emphasizing oneself.

0.1.n: が marks the speaker as the subject of being in those school years.

0.2.n: Combines with ３年生 to specify the school level.

0.3.n: 年生 indicates a student's year in school.

0.4.n: の connects the school-year description to 時, forming a phrase meaning when the speaker was that age.

0.5.n: 時 follows a description to express when something happened.

0.6.n: と joins the two periods in the speaker's school life.

0.8.n: 高校 is the usual shortened form of 高等学校.

0.9.n: Here this specifies the speaker's first year of high school.

0.10.n: の links １年生 to 時 to describe a particular period.

0.11.n: Together with 高校１年生の, this identifies when the speaker was in their first year of high school.

0.12.n: に marks the periods when the classes took place.

0.13.n: ちょうど emphasizes that the timing coincided with online classes.

0.14.n: This borrowed word describes how the classes were held.

0.15.n: で marks the method used for the classes, with the action continuing in the next line.

1.0.n: 授業 refers to school lessons rather than the group of students.

1.1.n: を marks 授業 as what the speaker did.

1.2.n: Past form of やる; 授業をやる casually describes participating in classes here.

1.3.n: After a past-form verb, こと helps form an expression about having done something before.

1.4.n: が marks こと as what exists in the pattern for having an experience.

1.5.n: ある completes やったことがある, expressing that the speaker has had this experience.

1.6.n: ん is shortened の and presents the statement as background information.

1.7.n: です makes the explanatory んです ending polite.

1.8.n: けど gently connects this background to what follows, without requiring a strong contrast.

2.0.n: ちょうど emphasizes that the classes coincided with the pandemic.

2.1.n: 禍 means calamity; コロナ禍 refers to the pandemic and its disruption.

2.2.n: で presents the pandemic as the circumstances surrounding the classes.

2.3.n: Past form of 受ける; with classes, it describes attending or receiving instruction.

2.4.n: の stands in for the classes the speaker took, turning 受けた into a noun-like phrase.

2.5.n: が marks 受けたの as what exists.

2.6.n: ある says there are classes fitting that description among the speaker's experiences.

2.7.n: ん adds an explanatory tone, clarifying the circumstances mentioned earlier.

2.8.n: です keeps the explanation polite.

3.0.n: その points back to the period of online classes.

3.1.n: その時 refers to the period just mentioned.

3.2.n: に marks when the connection problems occurred.

3.4.n: ネット is a common shortened form of インターネット.

3.5.n: の links the internet to its connection conditions.

3.6.n: 接続 combines with 環境 to describe the setup or conditions for connecting.

3.7.n: 環境 refers to the technical conditions affecting internet access here.

3.8.n: が marks the connection conditions as what was poor.

3.9.n: This is the portion of 悪い used before たり in 悪かったり, listing poor conditions as an example.

3.10.n: たり presents the poor connection as one example rather than an exhaustive description.

3.11.n: て-form of する completes たりして and connects these problems to the following consequences.

4.0.n: 先生 refers to the person teaching the online class.

4.1.n: の connects the teacher with what they were saying.

4.2.n: この points to the teacher's talk being discussed, without necessarily indicating anything physically nearby.

4.3.n: 話 refers to what the teacher was saying, not necessarily a story.

4.4.n: の links the teacher's talk to a portion of it.

4.5.n: 一部分 emphasizes that only some of the teacher's words were affected.

4.6.n: With a verb expressing ability, が can mark the thing the speaker could not catch.

4.7.n: ちょっと softens the description of the listening difficulty.

4.8.n: This is the negative past portion of 聞き取れる before たり; it describes being unable to make out spoken words.

4.9.n: たり lists not catching parts of the talk as one example of the difficulties.

0.lit: When I was a middle-school third-year student and a high-school first-year student, just then, online,
0.tip: School-year descriptions use の時に to say when something happened.

1.lit: Classes, I have the experience of doing, you see, but…
1.tip: A past-form verb plus ことがある means you have done something before.

2.lit: There are ones I took right during the COVID pandemic, you see.
2.tip: 受けたの means the ones I took, with の standing in for classes.

3.lit: At that time, the internet's connection conditions were bad and such, and…
3.tip: たりして presents a situation as one example and links it to what follows.

4.lit: A portion of this talk of the teacher's, I could not quite catch, and such…
4.tip: 聞き取れる means being able to make out spoken words; its negative describes difficulty catching what was said.
